subject: Urgent: Ecoshop inference slowdown & 5xx spike — impact analysis
messages:
From: Adam Lewis <adam.lewis@ecoshop.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: support@ecoshop.com
Date: 2027-12-04T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: High latency + 5xx on inference calls during checkout spikes

Hi Sofia,

We're seeing a recurring problem this morning across several checkout sessions where our calls to Redwood's /generate endpoint spike from ~80ms to 1.8s and intermittently return 502/504. It started around 07:50 PT and correlates with a traffic surge (~3x baseline). Attached are a short set of client-side logs and sample request IDs (ecoshop_error_samples.log).

Symptoms we've observed:
- 20-30% increase in median latency for inference calls for ~15 minutes in repeated bursts
- 502 and 504 responses tied to the same request IDs in the logs
- Traces show long DNS resolution times (~300-600ms) and several TCP retries before failure

This is impacting our checkout conversion. Can you confirm whether there's any known peering/egress issue or proxy throttling on your side? We broadly suspect a path problem (VPC peering or NAT limits on your egress proxies) because internal retries show different routes when successful.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and whether we should throttle from our side as a short-term mitigation.

Thanks,
Adam Lewis
Senior SRE, Ecoshop
adam.lewis@ecoshop.com

Forwarding Adam's report and logs. Executive summary for ops:

On 2027-12-04 07:50–08:10 PT Ecoshop experienced a ~3x traffic surge and reported: median inference latency increase (~80ms -> 1.8s), 502/504 responses, DNS resolution times of 300–600ms, TCP retries. They provided client-side logs and sample request IDs.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: check egress peering metrics (BGP flap, path changes) and DNS resolver error/latency graphs for the us-west region for that timeframe.
- Vanessa: review proxy pool utilization and NAT/conntrack metrics for the tenant namespace associated with Ecoshop; check per-tenant connection caps and queueing.
- Marissa: be prepared to own customer comms post-bridge; assemble a succinct timeline and impact statement for leadership.

Potential causes (to triage in parallel):
1) Resolver saturation or misconfigured resolver affinity causing high DNS latencies.
2) VPC peering route asymmetry or transient BGP flap leading to longer path and retries.
3) Proxy/NAT conntrack exhaustion or per-tenant connection throttling causing 502/504s.
4) Firewall/ACL edge rule misclassification kicking in during high connection churn.

Temporary mitigations to consider (if confirmed):
- Increase DNS resolver cache TTL and route certain prefixes to alternate resolvers; enable client-side retry jitter.
- Expand proxy worker pool or enable fallback to secondary egress route.
- Short-term per-tenant soft rate-limit to smooth burst.

Please post findings in the thread as soon as you have samples. I'm scheduling a bridge at 09:00 PT; Adam prefers phone/Zoom.

— Sofia

Date: 2027-12-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency + 5xx on inference calls during checkout spikes

Quick findings from first-pass triage (09:00–09:10 PT):

What I checked:
- BGP/peering: no long-lived BGP sessions down in us-west but we did see short path changes in AS path for one transit at 07:49:23 (single-hop reroute) lasting ~18s. Not catastrophic but worth flagging.
- DNS: our egress resolver pool had a sharp increase in query rate at 07:50; several resolvers show CPU spikes and queueing, correlating to the 300–600ms resolution seen in the traces. One resolver instance reported 5xx errors to the internal healthcheck and was restarted by autoscaler.
- Proxy/NAT: per-tenant conntrack usage for Ecoshop namespace hit 92% of threshold for a subset of proxy nodes; a downstream proxy returned intermittent 502s when it hit conntrack high water.

Likely root contributors (ordered):
1) Resolver pool stress combined with an autoscaler restart created transient DNS latency window.
2) High-connection churn during the spike pushed a handful of proxy nodes near conntrack limits producing 502s for in-flight connections.
3) A brief transit path change introduced additional RTT but not enough alone to cause 1.8s latencies.

Immediate remediation applied (09:05–09:10 PT):
- Increased resolver pool capacity + pinned critical resolvers for Ecoshop traffic for short term.
- Bumped conntrack threshold on the affected proxies and drained the two most saturated nodes.
- Enabled short-lived per-proxy connection shedding to avoid full failure (soft limit).

Next steps (owner assignments):
- vanessa_ortiz: review and provision longer-term conntrack increases and evaluate connection pooling improvements.
- marissa_cole: draft a customer-facing incident note and prepare SLO impact calc.
- sofia_ivanova: coordinate bridge and exec summary, decide on credit/contract remediation if needed.

I've opened INF-8421 for follow-up actions and a postmortem. Early indicator: mitigation reduced 5xxs by ~90% within 5 minutes; latencies returned toward baseline after resolver capacity increase and node drainage.

— Rishi
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Related ticket: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-8421

Hi Ben / product team — short executive note to flag customer impact and ask for decisions on credits/SLA remediation.

Summary:
- Customer: Ecoshop (large checkout traffic spikes)
- Window: 07:50–09:10 PT (peak impact 07:50–08:10)
- Impact: transient 502/504 responses causing checkout errors and ~3x latency spikes for a subset of requests; conversion impact reported by customer.
- Root causes (initial): resolver pool stress + conntrack pressure on several proxy nodes; brief transit path change contributed to increased RTT.
- Remediation applied: increased resolver capacity, drained saturated proxy nodes, bumped temporary conntrack thresholds, enabled soft-shedding. 5xxs reduced ~90% within 5 minutes of mitigation.

Request for leadership:
1) Approval to offer a one-time service credit for the impacted window pending postmortem (recommendation: 5% of monthly invoice pro-rated to incident duration).
2) Fast-track INF-8421 follow-up actions (conntrack limits, connection pooling, stronger resolver autoscaling) with target completion in 2 sprints.
3) Permission to send a tight customer incident summary (I'll draft) and offer a technical postmortem once complete.

Customer comms: Marissa — please prepare a 3–4 bullet incident summary and impact calc for Olivia (CSM) to send to Ecoshop.

I'll keep updates coming; we can discuss in the 16:00 leadership sync if helpful.

— Sofia Ivanova
